_about: Curated seed list: places you'd centre a ski trip around. Edit freely. category: resort | freeride | touring. level (resort only): all | advanced. tags: daytour (human-powered from a base), novelty (go for the place), heli, cat, boat, huts, volcano, spring, expedition, park. season/best are month numbers (season [start,end] may wrap the year). refElev = elevation (m) used for snow modelling. crowds 1 (empty) - 5 (lines). advisory = travel-advisory warning shown in the app. cost 1-5 = rough all-in cost per day for the usual way people do it (1 <$150, 2 $150-300, 3 $300-600, 4 $600-1,200, 5 $1,200+/day or $10k+ trips); self-guided touring is rated self-guided. pass = multi-resort pass affiliation, changes yearly: verify before relying on it. zone = map grouping (see zones); macro = world-view grouping.

destinations.name: Whistler Blackcomb
destinations.crowdNote: Huge terrain absorbs people, but village-gondola queues and the Sea-to-Sky drive get busy on weekends/holidays.
destinations.pitch: North America's biggest ski area: two mountains, 3,300+ ha, glaciers on top, rain risk at the base.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime: storm slabs and wind slabs dominate; generally fewer persistent layers than the interior.
destinations.weather: Wet, mild coastal storms; freezing levels can spike.

children.name: Spearhead Traverse
children.note: Classic hut traverse that starts from the lifts.

destinations.name: Lake Tahoe
destinations.crowdNote: Bay Area weekend crowds: Palisades lift lines and I-80 traffic on powder days are notorious. Go midweek.
destinations.pitch: A cluster of big resorts around the lake: huge snowfall years, sunny between storms, and very variable from season to season.
destinations.avalanche: Sierra maritime: big storm cycles, mostly storm/wind slabs; usually stabilises quickly.
destinations.weather: Feast-or-famine: atmospheric rivers bring metres of 'Sierra cement', then long sunny dry spells.

children.name: Sugar Bowl
children.note: Highest snowfall at the crest, less busy.

children.name: Heavenly
children.note: South Lake, lake views, nightlife, Epic.

children.name: Kirkwood
children.note: Remote, steep, deep. Advanced skiers' choice, Epic.

children.name: Mt Rose
children.note: High base, close to Reno, the Chutes.

destinations.name: Mammoth Mountain
destinations.crowdNote: LA weekend crowds; midweek is quiet.
destinations.pitch: High-altitude volcano with one of the longest seasons in the US, often into June.
destinations.avalanche: Sierra maritime/transitional: big storm cycles bring storm and wind slabs that usually settle within days; wet slides in spring.
destinations.weather: Big storms then intense sun; wind is a factor at the top.

destinations.name: Cottonwood Canyons (Alta, Snowbird, Brighton, Solitude)
destinations.crowdNote: Snow is legendary but the canyon road is a parking lot on powder mornings (the 'Red Snake'). Interlodge closures happen.
destinations.pitch: 'Greatest Snow on Earth': light, frequent lake-effect snow and steep terrain, 40 minutes from a major airport.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain: often a buried persistent weak layer from early-season facets.
destinations.weather: Frequent cold storms; dry, light snow.

destinations.name: Park City & Deer Valley
destinations.crowdNote: Big but busy, especially holidays.
destinations.pitch: The US's largest single resort plus Deer Valley's luxury groomers; a real town with food and nightlife. Family-friendly.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain: early-season facets can leave a buried persistent weak layer; the backcountry gates off the resorts see serious slides.
destinations.weather: Less snow than the Cottonwoods; sunny.

destinations.name: Jackson Hole
destinations.crowdNote: Tram line on powder days; otherwise manageable.
destinations.pitch: Steep, big-vertical resort with Corbet's Couloir and world-class sidecountry; Grand Targhee next door for deep snow.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain/continental: persistent slabs are common in the Tetons.
destinations.weather: Cold; storms off the Pacific, deep at Targhee.

children.name: Grand Targhee
children.note: West side of the Tetons: deeper, cheaper, mellow.

destinations.name: Big Sky
destinations.crowdNote: Lots of acres per skier.
destinations.pitch: Huge, uncrowded terrain under Lone Peak's steep tram line.
destinations.avalanche: Continental: cold, shallow snowpack with persistent weak layers.
destinations.weather: Cold, drier snow, windy summit.

destinations.name: Aspen Snowmass
destinations.crowdNote: Four mountains spread people out.
destinations.pitch: Four mountains (Snowmass, Ajax, Highlands, Buttermilk) and a glamorous town; Highland Bowl hike for experts.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: deep persistent slabs a recurring theme.
destinations.weather: Sunny, cold, dry snow.

children.name: Aspen Mountain (Ajax)
children.note: Steep groomers above town, no beginner terrain.

destinations.name: Vail & Beaver Creek
destinations.crowdNote: Front Range I-70 crowds and weekend lines.
destinations.pitch: Massive groomed front side plus the Back Bowls; polished, expensive resort villages.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: cold, shallow early snowpack builds facets, so deep persistent slabs are a recurring winter-long problem off-piste.
destinations.weather: Sunny, cold, light snow.

children.name: Vail
children.note: Front side plus the Back Bowls.

destinations.name: Summit County (Breckenridge, Keystone, A-Basin, Copper)
destinations.crowdNote: Closest big resorts to Denver: heavy weekend traffic.
destinations.pitch: High-altitude cluster with lots of choice; A-Basin skis into June.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: weak, faceted base layers are common and persistent slabs can stay reactive all season outside the resorts.
destinations.weather: High, cold, windy at the top, sunny.

destinations.name: Steamboat
destinations.pitch: 'Champagne powder' and famous tree skiing; ranch-town feel.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental, though wetter than most of the state: persistent weak layers still form in thin early winters.
destinations.weather: Frequent light snowfall, cold.

destinations.name: Telluride
destinations.crowdNote: Remote: rarely a line.
destinations.pitch: Stunning box canyon town with a mix of family groomers and hike-to expert terrain.
destinations.avalanche: San Juan continental: some of the weakest snowpacks in the US.
destinations.weather: Sunny, dry, cold.

destinations.name: Crested Butte
destinations.pitch: Funky old mining town; the Extreme Limits are among the steepest lift-served terrain in the US.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: shallow, faceted snowpack with persistent slabs; the Elk Mountains have a serious avalanche history.
destinations.weather: Cold, sunny.

destinations.name: Taos Ski Valley
destinations.pitch: Steep, high, sunny; hike-to Kachina and Highline ridges. Adobe culture.
destinations.avalanche: Southern Rockies continental: often thin and faceted, with persistent slabs; dry spells between storms weaken the snowpack further.
destinations.weather: Southwestern sun, variable snow years.

destinations.name: Sun Valley
destinations.pitch: America's first destination resort: long consistent fall-line groomers on Bald Mountain.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain: a mix of storm slabs and persistent weak layers; the backcountry around Ketchum is forecast by the Sawtooth center.
destinations.weather: Sunny, modest snowfall.

destinations.name: Alyeska
destinations.pitch: Sea-level base and steep upper bowls; pairs with Turnagain Pass touring and Chugach heli.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal Alaska maritime: heavy storms and strong winds build deep storm and wind slabs; short days, rain-on-snow events possible.
destinations.weather: Short days midwinter, wet coastal storms.

destinations.name: Mt. Baker
destinations.crowdNote: Seattle weekends.
destinations.pitch: Record-holding snowfall, rustic lifts, and sidecountry and backcountry access off the top. Core skier culture.
destinations.avalanche: Cascade maritime: storm slabs, deep heavy snow.
destinations.weather: Very wet, heavy snow; often stormy.

destinations.name: Silverton Mountain
destinations.crowdNote: Guided-only days cap numbers.
destinations.pitch: One chairlift, all expert, avalanche-gear-required, mostly guided. Optional heli drops.
destinations.avalanche: San Juan continental: notoriously weak snowpack.
destinations.weather: High altitude, cold, sunny between storms.

destinations.name: Revelstoke
destinations.crowdNote: Getting busier, but still modest.
destinations.pitch: Biggest lift-served vertical in North America (1,713 m); hub for cat and heli skiing and Rogers Pass.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC transitional: buried surface hoar a classic problem.
destinations.weather: Deep, frequent snowfall, often cloudy.

destinations.name: Kicking Horse
destinations.pitch: Steep chutes and big bowls above Golden; on the Powder Highway with Revelstoke.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC/Rockies transitional: buried surface hoar and facets are common persistent layers, so off-piste needs care all season.
destinations.weather: Drier, colder than the coast.

destinations.name: Fernie
destinations.crowdNote: Calgary weekends.
destinations.pitch: Five big alpine bowls and lots of snow in a historic town.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC: big snowfall with buried surface hoar layers that can linger for weeks; storm slabs after each cycle.
destinations.weather: Big snowfall, mild by Rockies standards.

destinations.name: Kootenays (Red Mountain & Whitewater)
destinations.crowdNote: Tiny crowds.
destinations.pitch: Old-school, steep tree skiing in Rossland and Nelson; lots of cat skiing nearby.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC: buried surface hoar and storm slabs are the classic problems; the slackcountry beyond the ropes is serious terrain.
destinations.weather: Frequent snow, often cloudy.

children.name: RED Mountain (Rossland)
children.note: Steep trees, two mountains, cat skiing.

children.name: Whitewater (Nelson)
children.note: Small, deep, great food, cool town.

destinations.name: Banff (Lake Louise, Sunshine, Norquay)
destinations.pitch: Three resorts inside a national park; spectacular scenery, cold, long season.
destinations.avalanche: Rockies continental: weak, faceted base layers are typical.
destinations.weather: Cold (−20s °C), dry snow.

children.name: Sunshine Village
children.note: Snowiest of the three; Delirium Dive.

destinations.name: Big White
destinations.pitch: Family ski-in/ski-out village with dry 'champagne powder'; famous for fog (snow ghosts).
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC (Okanagan): lighter snowfall than the Kootenays, with surface hoar layers possible; mostly gentle in-bounds terrain.
destinations.weather: Often foggy, light snow.

destinations.name: Mont-Tremblant
destinations.crowdNote: Holiday and weekend crowds from Montreal.
destinations.pitch: Eastern North America's flagship resort village with French-Canadian charm.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resort, avalanche risk is minimal (low-angle, treed eastern terrain). No regular avalanche forecast is needed here.
destinations.weather: Cold, icy days possible; freeze-thaw.

destinations.name: Northern Vermont (Stowe, Jay Peak, Sugarbush)
destinations.crowdNote: Holiday weekends busy.
destinations.pitch: Best snow in the US Northeast; classic New England tree skiing.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resorts, avalanche risk is minimal. Steeper slides and gullies (e.g. Smugglers' Notch) can avalanche after big storms.
destinations.weather: Cold, variable, icy spells.

children.name: Jay Peak
children.note: Most snow in the East, glades.

destinations.name: Rogers Pass
destinations.crowdNote: Popular parking areas on sunny weekends; permit system (winter restricted areas).
destinations.airport: Calgary 4h / Kelowna 3h; base in Revelstoke or Golden
destinations.pitch: Iconic Selkirk backcountry on the Trans-Canada Highway: huge snowfall, glaciers, trees, and huts.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC: buried surface hoar and deep persistent layers; Parks Canada forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Stormy and deep; clear spells bring cold.

destinations.name: Interior BC Heli & Cat (Selkirks, Monashees, Bugaboos)
destinations.crowdNote: Lodge-based, small groups.
destinations.airport: Calgary / Kelowna, plus heli or road transfer
destinations.pitch: The birthplace of heli-skiing: endless old-growth tree runs and glaciers from remote lodges (CMH, Mike Wiegele, Baldface cat).
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC; operators run professional programs.
destinations.weather: Deep, cold-smoke powder; flying days lost to cloud.

destinations.name: Teton Pass & Grand Teton backcountry
destinations.crowdNote: Teton Pass road-side is heavily used.
destinations.pitch: Road-accessed touring off Teton Pass; spring ski mountaineering in Grand Teton NP.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain/continental: persistent slabs are common and the terrain is big and close to the road; the Bridger-Teton center forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Cold, frequent snow.

destinations.name: Chugach / Valdez Heli
destinations.pitch: The steep spines of ski films. Coastal Alaska snow sticks to 50° faces. Very weather-dependent.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime; sluff management, wind slabs; deep instabilities possible.
destinations.weather: Down days are common: budget them in.

destinations.name: Haines Heli
destinations.pitch: Alaska's other heli mecca: big glaciated lines, smaller and quieter than Valdez.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime: deep storm and wind slabs, big sluffs on steep faces; operators run professional avalanche programs.
destinations.weather: Very variable; down days.

destinations.name: Colorado Hut Systems (10th Mountain)
destinations.crowdNote: Huts book a year ahead via lottery.
destinations.pitch: Network of 30+ backcountry huts between Vail, Aspen and Leadville.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: deep persistent slabs. Conservative terrain choices matter.
destinations.weather: Cold, sunny, dry snow.

destinations.name: San Juans Backcountry (Red Mountain Pass)
destinations.pitch: High-alpine road-access touring between Silverton and Ouray, with yurts and huts.
destinations.avalanche: One of the weakest snowpacks anywhere: very conservative early season.
destinations.weather: High, cold, sunny.

destinations.name: Cascade Volcanoes (Hood, Rainier, Baker, Adams)
destinations.pitch: Spring corn-snow road trip, skiing big glaciated volcanoes from the summit.
destinations.avalanche: Spring snowpack: daily wet-snow cycles (start early, off before it softens), cornices, plus crevasses and icefall on the glaciers.
destinations.weather: Stable spring highs; storms off the Pacific.

destinations.name: Eastern Sierra Backcountry
destinations.pitch: Huge couloirs above Highway 395 (Bishop, June Lake, Mammoth); world-class spring corn.
destinations.avalanche: Sierra: big storms then stable; spring wet slides.
destinations.weather: Sunny, big storm cycles.

destinations.name: Mt Washington (Tuckerman Ravine)
destinations.crowdNote: Spring weekends are a scene.
destinations.pitch: Classic Eastern spring pilgrimage to the ravine headwall.
destinations.avalanche: Wind-loaded ravines; forecast by Mount Washington Avalanche Center.
destinations.weather: Notorious for extreme wind and weather.

destinations.name: Chic-Chocs (Gaspésie)
destinations.airport: Montréal, then a long drive / Mont-Joli
destinations.pitch: Eastern Canada's best snow: open alpine bowls above the St. Lawrence, with huts and lodges.
destinations.avalanche: Wind slabs and cornices; Avalanche Québec forecasts.
destinations.weather: Maritime, windy, frequent snow.

destinations.name: Portillo
destinations.crowdNote: Hotel-capped numbers.
destinations.pitch: Legendary single-hotel resort on Laguna del Inca; steep chutes like the Super C.
destinations.avalanche: Andean: big storm cycles, wind; can close the pass road.
destinations.weather: Sunny high Andes; storms close the road for days.

destinations.name: Santiago Three Valleys (Valle Nevado, La Parva, El Colorado)
destinations.crowdNote: Santiago weekends.
destinations.pitch: Big interconnected high-Andes terrain an hour from a capital city; heli-skiing on offer.
destinations.avalanche: High, dry Andes: strong winds build wind slabs; storm cycles are short and intense. Limited public forecasting.
destinations.weather: Mostly sunny; snow comes in a few big storms.

destinations.name: Las Leñas
destinations.crowdNote: Argentine winter holidays (July) get busy.
destinations.pitch: The Marte chair accesses vast steep chute terrain. Famous among freeriders, when Marte runs.
destinations.avalanche: Andean continental-ish: dry, wind-affected snowpack with wind slabs and some persistent layers; the Marte lift accesses big avalanche terrain.
destinations.weather: Wind often closes Marte; dry snow.

destinations.name: Nevados de Chillán
destinations.pitch: Volcano resort with hot springs and Chile's longest run; big sidecountry.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime Andes: wet, heavy storms bring storm slabs and rain-on-snow; volcanic terrain with big open slopes.
destinations.weather: Stormier and snowier than central Chile.

destinations.name: Bariloche (Cerro Catedral)
destinations.crowdNote: Very busy in July school holidays.
destinations.pitch: South America's largest resort over a Patagonian lake city; great sidecountry and Frey touring nearby.
destinations.avalanche: Patagonian maritime: wet storms and strong westerly winds bring storm and wind slabs; usually settles fast after storms.
destinations.weather: Variable, windy, mixed snow quality; lower base can be wet.

destinations.name: Bariloche Backcountry (Refugio Frey)
destinations.pitch: Granite spires and couloirs around Refugio Frey, accessed from Catedral.
destinations.avalanche: Patagonian maritime: wind and storm slabs dominate, with spring wet-snow cycles. No regular public forecast, so rely on local guides.
destinations.weather: Windy Patagonian weather windows.

destinations.name: Araucanía Volcanoes (Pucón)
destinations.pitch: Road trip skiing perfect volcanic cones (Villarrica, Llaima, Lonquimay) with hot springs and araucaria forests.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: spring corn cycles with wet slides in the afternoon, wind-scoured icy summits; crevasses on some glaciated cones.
destinations.weather: Storms then clear spells; spring is best.

children.name: Corralco (Lonquimay)
children.note: Lifts plus 3,000 ha of volcano backcountry.

destinations.name: Ushuaia (Cerro Castor)
destinations.pitch: The southernmost resort on Earth; low-elevation but dependable cold snow; backcountry touring around.
destinations.avalanche: Sub-Antarctic maritime: frequent storms, strong winds and wind slabs; temperatures hover near freezing.
destinations.weather: Cold, windy, short days.

destinations.name: Antarctic Peninsula (sail & ski)
destinations.crowdNote: A handful of yachts per season.
destinations.pitch: Ski from sea to summit from expedition yachts among icebergs and penguins. The trip of a lifetime.
destinations.avalanche: Glaciated; crevasses, wind slab; no forecasting service.
destinations.weather: Fast-changing maritime weather; Drake crossing can be rough.

destinations.name: Chamonix Mont-Blanc
destinations.crowdNote: Grands Montets and Aiguille du Midi queues on powder days.
destinations.pitch: The world capital of alpinism and freeride: Vallée Blanche, Grands Montets, huge glaciated terrain. Gateway to the Haute Route.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Alps: mix of wind slabs and persistent layers; glacier hazards.
destinations.weather: Big Atlantic storms, foehn; the valley floor is low (1,035 m).

destinations.name: La Grave – La Meije
destinations.crowdNote: A single téléphérique and no pisting: rarely busy.
destinations.pitch: Just a cable car and 2,000 m of ungroomed, glaciated high-mountain freeride. Mythic. Pairs with Serre Chevalier.
destinations.avalanche: Southern French Alps: thinner snowpack, persistent layers possible.
destinations.weather: Sunny but winds close the lift; storms from both north and south.

destinations.name: Les 3 Vallées (Courchevel, Méribel, Val Thorens)
destinations.crowdNote: February French school holidays are rammed.
destinations.pitch: The world's largest linked ski area (600 km of pistes); ski-in/ski-out at altitude.
destinations.avalanche: Northern French Alps: wind slabs and persistent layers in thin winters. In-bounds is controlled, but the off-piste is vast and not.
destinations.weather: High altitude (Val Thorens 2,300 m) keeps snow reliable.

destinations.name: Val d'Isère & Tignes
destinations.pitch: High, snow-sure, and legendary off-piste (Espace Killy); glacier skiing at Tignes.
destinations.avalanche: Inner Alps-ish; persistent layers often present.
destinations.weather: Often catches 'retour d'Est' storms from Italy.

destinations.name: Paradiski (Les Arcs, La Plagne)
destinations.pitch: Huge linked area with purpose-built villages; very family-friendly; train-accessible.
destinations.avalanche: Northern French Alps: wind and storm slabs, persistent layers in thin winters. Off-piste is big and uncontrolled; the BRA forecast covers it.

destinations.name: Portes du Soleil (Avoriaz, Morzine, Champéry)
destinations.pitch: Cross-border circuit of 12 resorts; lower altitude, so check snow conditions.
destinations.avalanche: Pre-Alps, lower and wetter: storm slabs and wet-snow problems more than deep persistent layers. Off-piste is uncontrolled.
destinations.weather: Lower-altitude rain risk.

destinations.name: Alpe d'Huez
destinations.pitch: Sunny south-facing giant with the 16 km Sarenne black run.
destinations.avalanche: Western French Alps: wind slabs and persistent layers in thin winters; big off-piste (e.g. La Sarenne) is uncontrolled.
destinations.weather: Sunny.

destinations.name: Verbier (4 Vallées)
destinations.crowdNote: Mont Fort and the Tortin lifts get crowded.
destinations.pitch: Freeride capital (Xtreme Verbier); off-piste right off the lifts, plus a huge linked piste network.
destinations.avalanche: Valais inner-Alpine: persistent weak layers common in thin winters.
destinations.weather: Drier inner-Alpine climate, sunny.

destinations.name: Zermatt (+ Cervinia)
destinations.pitch: Car-free village under the Matterhorn, glacier skiing, and lunch in Italy. End of the Haute Route.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine (Valais): often thin, faceted snowpack with persistent weak layers; glacier hazards (crevasses) off-piste.
destinations.weather: Dry, sunny; one of the highest areas in the Alps.

destinations.name: Saas-Fee
destinations.pitch: Glacier village surrounded by thirteen 4,000 m peaks; snow-sure and quieter than Zermatt.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine (Valais) and glaciated: persistent weak layers in thin winters, crevasses off-piste; SLF forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Catches southern storms.

destinations.name: Engelberg
destinations.crowdNote: Titlis tourists, but freeride lines quiet.
destinations.pitch: Titlis' 2,000 m freeride descents (Laub, Galtiberg); a Scandinavian freeride community; easy from Zurich.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Alps: big snowfalls bring storm and wind slabs; the famous Titlis off-piste is serious, glaciated avalanche terrain.
destinations.weather: Northern stau: frequent snow, also fog.

destinations.name: Andermatt
destinations.pitch: Gemsstock's steep freeride terrain at a snow crossroads catching storms from north and south.
destinations.avalanche: Central Alps, very snowy: frequent storm and wind slabs; the Gemsstock is steep, freeride-heavy avalanche terrain.
destinations.weather: Snowy: storms from both sides.

destinations.name: St. Moritz & Engadin
destinations.pitch: Sunny high valley with Corviglia, Diavolezza glacier runs, and glamour.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine (Engadin): dry, cold and often thin, so weak faceted layers and persistent slabs are common. SLF forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Very sunny, cold, dry.

destinations.name: Davos Klosters
destinations.pitch: Five ski areas, long off-piste descents to villages, home of the SLF avalanche institute.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine (Graubünden): persistent weak layers are common in thin winters; the SLF avalanche institute is based here.

children.name: Parsenn (Davos)
children.note: Biggest area, long runs to Klosters.

destinations.name: Laax Flims
destinations.pitch: Europe's freestyle capital: huge terrain parks, and a glacier.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Graubünden, between the northern Alps and inner-Alpine zone: wind slabs and some persistent layers; off-piste is uncontrolled.

destinations.name: Jungfrau Region (Wengen, Grindelwald, Mürren)
destinations.pitch: Car-free villages under the Eiger; the scenery is the point.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Alps: heavy snowfall with storm and wind slabs; usually fewer deep persistent problems than the inner-Alpine regions.
destinations.weather: Lower bases; northern stau storms.

children.name: Grindelwald
children.note: Under the Eiger, First and Männlichen.

destinations.name: Arlberg (St. Anton, Lech, Zürs)
destinations.pitch: Birthplace of Alpine skiing: steep ungroomed 'ski routes', big off-piste, and legendary après.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Alps, very snowy: frequent storm and wind slabs. Huge, popular off-piste that sees accidents every winter.
destinations.weather: Northern stau makes it one of the snowiest areas in Austria.

destinations.name: Ischgl & Paznaun
destinations.pitch: Cross-border to Samnaun (Switzerland); high, snow-sure, party town.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine (Tyrol): colder and drier than the northern Alps, so persistent weak layers are common in thin winters. Off-piste is uncontrolled.

destinations.name: Ötztal (Sölden, Obergurgl)
destinations.pitch: Two glaciers and Austria's most reliable snow; Obergurgl is quiet and family-oriented.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine: dry, often thin snowpack with persistent weak layers; glacier hazards off-piste at Sölden.
destinations.weather: Dry inner-Alpine climate, high altitude.

destinations.name: Kitzbühel & SkiWelt
destinations.pitch: Historic town, the Streif, and a huge linked area; low altitude, so check snow conditions.
destinations.avalanche: Lower northern Alps: storm slabs and wet-snow problems more than deep persistent layers. Little high, steep terrain off-piste.
destinations.weather: Low elevation: rain risk.

destinations.name: Zillertal (Mayrhofen, Hintertux)
destinations.pitch: A valley of linked areas, with year-round glacier skiing at Hintertux.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Tyrol, with high glacier terrain at Hintertux: wind slabs and persistent layers; crevasses on the glacier off-piste.

destinations.name: Saalbach Hinterglemm
destinations.pitch: Big, cruisy ski circus with lively après.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Alps, mid-altitude: storm slabs and wet-snow problems; off-piste is moderate but still avalanche terrain.
destinations.weather: Lower: rain risk.

destinations.name: Dolomiti Superski (Val Gardena, Alta Badia, Cortina)
destinations.crowdNote: Sella Ronda can be congested.
destinations.pitch: 1,200 km of pistes in UNESCO limestone towers, with incredible food and huts. Sunny cruising; snowmaking-reliant.
destinations.avalanche: Southern Alps: often thin, faceted snowpack with persistent weak layers; steep couloirs and gullies concentrate risk.
destinations.weather: Very sunny, dry; depends on southern storms.

destinations.name: Courmayeur & Skyway
destinations.pitch: Italian side of Mont Blanc: Skyway Monte Bianco gives big glacier freeride; great food; 20 min from Chamonix.
destinations.avalanche: Southern side of Mont Blanc, glaciated: big southern storms bring heavy slabs; crevasses and seracs on the Skyway off-piste.
destinations.weather: Catches southern (retour d'Est) storms when Chamonix misses.

destinations.name: Monte Rosa (Alagna, Gressoney)
destinations.pitch: Alagna is a freeride mecca: few pistes, huge lift-served off-piste, legal heli drops.
destinations.avalanche: Southern Alps, high and glaciated: persistent layers in thin winters, wind slabs, crevasses. Off-piste is serious, guided terrain.
destinations.weather: Southern storms.

destinations.name: Livigno
destinations.pitch: High, cold, duty-free valley, snow-sure with great parks.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine (Lombardy): cold, dry, often thin snowpack with persistent weak layers; off-piste is uncontrolled.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry.

destinations.name: Grandvalira
destinations.pitch: The Pyrenees' largest area, good value, and duty-free shopping.
destinations.avalanche: Eastern Pyrenees: wind slabs and wet-snow cycles; snowfall is variable and the snowpack can be thin. Off-piste is uncontrolled.
destinations.weather: Sunny; Mediterranean storms.

destinations.name: Baqueira-Beret
destinations.crowdNote: Spanish holidays busy.
destinations.pitch: Spain's best resort, on the Atlantic-facing Pyrenees with good off-piste.
destinations.avalanche: Central Pyrenees (Aran): Atlantic storms bring storm and wind slabs; wet slides in spring. Local bulletin covers the Aran valley.
destinations.weather: Atlantic storms.

destinations.name: Haute Route (Chamonix → Zermatt)
destinations.crowdNote: Huts book out months ahead in April.
destinations.pitch: The classic 6-7 day hut-to-hut glacier traverse. Bucket list.
destinations.avalanche: High-alpine glaciated; spring cycles; crevasses.
destinations.weather: Weather windows decide everything.

destinations.name: Silvretta & Rätikon huts
destinations.pitch: Friendly glaciated hut touring with lots of 3,000 m peaks; good first hut trip.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine: dry, often thin snowpack with persistent weak layers; wind slabs on lee slopes and glacier hazards above the huts.

destinations.name: Ötztal Alps huts (Vent)
destinations.pitch: High glaciated hut tours to the Wildspitze, Austria's second-highest peak.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine: dry, often thin snowpack with persistent weak layers; glaciers and crevasses throughout the hut terrain.
destinations.weather: Dry, sunny.

destinations.name: Gran Paradiso
destinations.pitch: A 'ski-able' 4,000er from the Vittorio Emanuele hut, in a national park full of ibex.
destinations.avalanche: Western Alps, glaciated: wind slabs and spring wet-snow cycles; crevasses on the approach to the summit.

destinations.name: Riksgränsen
destinations.crowdNote: Busy for the Scandinavian Big Mountain event and late May.
destinations.pitch: Arctic freeride: skiing under the midnight sun in May-June, plus heli. A train station on the slope.
destinations.avalanche: Arctic coastal: wind slabs dominate on open, treeless terrain; long spring days bring wet-snow cycles in May and June.
destinations.weather: Polar night until Feb; best light in spring; wind.

destinations.name: Kebnekaise & Abisko
destinations.pitch: Sweden's highest peak and arctic hut tours along the Kungsleden.
destinations.avalanche: Sub-arctic continental: cold, thin snowpack with facets and wind slabs; sparse forecasting, so local knowledge matters.
destinations.weather: Cold, windy, aurora.

children.name: Kungsleden (winter)
children.note: Hut-to-hut classic; Sarek is the wild step up.

destinations.name: Åre
destinations.crowdNote: Swedish sport holidays (Feb-Mar).
destinations.airport: Åre Östersund (OSD), 1.5h; night train from Stockholm
destinations.pitch: Scandinavia's biggest resort; lively village, off-piste on the top.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resort, controlled. Off-piste: wind slabs on open, treeless upper slopes; lavinprognoser.se covers the area.
destinations.weather: Short, cold days in midwinter; longer spring days.

destinations.name: Hemsedal
destinations.crowdNote: Easter is peak.
destinations.pitch: Norway's leading resort, the 'Scandinavian Alps'; family plus decent steeps.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resort, controlled. Off-piste: wind slabs and persistent layers in cold spells; varsom.no forecasts the region.
destinations.weather: Cold.

destinations.name: Lyngen Alps
destinations.crowdNote: Popular, but fjord coastline spreads people out.
destinations.pitch: The original sea-to-summit arctic touring: 1,500 m runs to the fjord, by lodge, ferry, or sailboat.
destinations.avalanche: Arctic coastal: wind slabs; persistent layers in colder years; varsom.no forecasts.
destinations.weather: Coastal arctic: fast-changing, long spring daylight.

destinations.name: Lofoten
destinations.pitch: Dramatic peaks out of the sea; boat-based touring and fishing villages.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime arctic: frequent storms, strong winds and wind slabs; steep slopes run straight into the sea.
destinations.weather: Mild for the latitude; wet storms, shifting conditions.

destinations.name: Senja
destinations.pitch: Norway's second-largest island: quieter alternative to Lyngen.
destinations.avalanche: Arctic coastal: wind slabs and storm slabs on steep coastal peaks; spring wet-snow cycles.

destinations.name: Narvikfjellet
destinations.pitch: Lift-accessed, steep fjord freeride above town; combine with Riksgränsen.
destinations.avalanche: Arctic coastal: wind slabs on open terrain above the trees; the off-piste from the top lift is steep and committing.

destinations.name: Sunnmøre Alps
destinations.pitch: Fjord-to-summit classic (Hjørundfjord, Slogen) with historic hotels and boat access.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: storm and wind slabs, then spring wet-snow cycles on steep fjord-side slopes. varsom.no forecasts the region.
destinations.weather: Wet, variable; spring is reliable.

destinations.name: Romsdal (Åndalsnes)
destinations.pitch: Big-wall valley with steep couloirs and fjord descents.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: storm and wind slabs; steep, big terrain above the fjord, with wet slides in spring.

destinations.name: Svalbard
destinations.pitch: High-arctic ski expeditions by boat or snowmobile: glaciers, polar bears (armed guides required).
destinations.avalanche: Polar: thin, wind-affected snowpack with wind slabs and weak bases; glaciers, crevasses and polar bears add to the hazards.
destinations.weather: Cold, 24h daylight from late April.

permits.label: Travel rules and notification (Governor of Svalbard)

destinations.name: Troll Peninsula
destinations.pitch: Peak-to-ocean heli and touring with long spring daylight and hot pools.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime sub-arctic: wind slabs and storm slabs; spring wet-snow cycles. The Icelandic Met Office forecasts north Iceland.
destinations.weather: Very changeable; down days likely.

destinations.name: Westfjords
destinations.pitch: Remote, sailboat-based fjord touring.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: frequent storms, wind slabs and cornices; spring wet-snow cycles. Settlements here have a long avalanche history.
destinations.weather: Wild, windy.

destinations.name: West Greenland (Maniitsoq & Sisimiut)
destinations.airport: Kangerlussuaq / Nuuk, then boat or heli
destinations.pitch: Expedition-yacht and heli skiing in empty fjords. Maniitsoq is called the 'Venice of the Arctic'.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecasting service: wind slabs dominate on open slopes, with spring wet-snow cycles. Go guided.
destinations.weather: Cold, stable spring highs; long days.

destinations.name: East Greenland (Tasiilaq)
destinations.pitch: The Ammassalik Alps: jagged peaks and sea ice; very remote.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecasting service: wind slabs and cornices on steep coastal peaks, glaciers in places. Go guided.
destinations.weather: Piteraq winds can be severe.

destinations.name: Gudauri
destinations.pitch: Open, treeless freeride and cheap heli on the Georgian Military Highway; amazing food and wine.
destinations.avalanche: Caucasus: wind slabs on big, open, treeless slopes; persistent layers in thin winters. Freeride accidents are common, so hire a guide.
destinations.weather: Snowy, can be windy.

destinations.name: Svaneti (Mestia & Tetnuldi)
destinations.pitch: Medieval tower villages under 4,000-5,000 m Caucasus peaks; touring off small lifts.
destinations.avalanche: Caucasus: heavy snowfalls, wind slabs and persistent layers; big terrain with limited forecasting. Go guided.

destinations.name: Kaçkar Mountains Heli
destinations.pitch: Black Sea moisture onto the Pontic Alps: deep snow, lodge heli skiing.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime (Black Sea): heavy, wet snowfall with storm slabs; the heli operator runs its own avalanche program.
destinations.weather: Wet Black Sea storms.

destinations.name: Gulmarg
destinations.pitch: Himalayan gondola to almost 4,000 m with vast freeride for little money.
destinations.avalanche: Himalayan: big storms, persistent layers; limited forecasting.
destinations.weather: Western disturbances bring big dumps.
destinations.advisory: Some governments advise against travel to parts of Jammu & Kashmir. Check your government's current advice and your insurance.

destinations.name: Karakol & Tian Shan
destinations.pitch: Adventure: a small resort plus yurt-based touring and cat skiing in dry continental powder.
destinations.avalanche: Continental: cold, thin snowpack with depth hoar and a weak base; deep persistent slabs. Limited forecasting, so go with local guides.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry.

destinations.name: Kamchatka Heli
destinations.pitch: Heli-skiing volcanoes that run down to the Pacific: one of the wildest heli destinations on Earth.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime volcanic: deep storm and wind slabs, big open volcano slopes; the heli operators manage avalanche risk.
destinations.weather: Pacific storms.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

destinations.name: Niseko & Rusutsu
destinations.crowdNote: Very international and busy now: Hirafu lift lines, booked-out restaurants, Western prices.
destinations.pitch: JAPOW ground zero: relentless light snow off the Sea of Japan, gate-controlled off-piste, onsens.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime, often deep-snow cycles; Niseko local avalanche rules apply.
destinations.weather: Grey and snowing most days in Jan; cold, not much sun.

children.name: Niseko United (Grand Hirafu, Annupuri, Village, Hanazono)

destinations.name: Kiroro & Sapporo resorts
destinations.crowdNote: Quieter than Niseko.
destinations.pitch: Kiroro is one of Hokkaido's deepest snow spots; Teine/Kokusai are day trips from Sapporo city.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime (Hokkaido west coast): frequent storm slabs from daily snowfall; tree wells and sluffs off-piste.
destinations.weather: Very snowy.

destinations.name: Furano & Central Hokkaido (Tomamu, Kamui)
destinations.crowdNote: Much more Japanese than Niseko.
destinations.pitch: Colder, drier inland Hokkaido powder; mix of resorts and a road trip to Asahidake.
destinations.avalanche: Inland Hokkaido: colder and drier, so facets and buried weak layers can form; storm slabs after big snowfalls.
destinations.weather: Coldest and driest snow in Japan.

destinations.name: Asahidake
destinations.crowdNote: One ropeway: queues on powder mornings.
destinations.pitch: A single ropeway up Hokkaido's highest (steaming) volcano: ungroomed, ultra-dry powder in birch forest.
destinations.avalanche: Cold inland snowpack; volcano terrain; whiteouts.
destinations.weather: Cold and stormy; navigation is hard in whiteout.

destinations.name: Tokachi & Daisetsuzan Backcountry
destinations.pitch: Hut-based and road-access touring (Fukiage, Sandan-yama) in famously dry snow.
destinations.avalanche: Cold inland Hokkaido: persistent weak layers (facets, surface hoar) are more common than on the coast; storm slabs after big dumps.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry.

destinations.name: Hakuba Valley
destinations.crowdNote: Westernised and busy at Happo-one; quieter at Cortina/Norikura.
destinations.pitch: Ten resorts under the Northern Alps, Olympic heritage, and serious backcountry in the Hakuba mountains.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime Honshu: very heavy snowfall loads slopes fast, so storm slabs and glide cracks; big alpine terrain above the resorts.
destinations.weather: Heavy snowfall but milder than Hokkaido: rain risk at the base later in the season.

destinations.name: Myoko, Nozawa & Shiga Kogen
destinations.crowdNote: More Japanese, more traditional than Hakuba/Niseko.
destinations.pitch: Onsen villages (Nozawa), Japan's largest linked area (Shiga), and Myoko/Lotte Arai's deep snow.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime Honshu: very heavy loading brings storm slabs; tree wells and glide avalanches. Off-piste needs gate rules and care.
destinations.weather: Very snowy (Myoko), heavier snow than Hokkaido.

children.name: Shiga Kogen
children.note: Japan's largest linked area, high and dry.

destinations.name: Hakkoda & Tohoku
destinations.pitch: A ropeway into backcountry known for 'snow monsters' (rime-coated trees); deep, cold and few foreigners. Pair with Zao.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: heavy snowfall, tree wells and navigation in flat light are bigger day-to-day issues than slabs; storm slabs after dumps.
destinations.weather: Cold, stormy, whiteouts.

children.name: Gassan
children.note: Spring-only ski area (Apr–Jul) with famous touring.

children.name: Chōkai
children.note: Coastal volcano; long spring runs to the Sea of Japan.

destinations.name: L+SNOW Shanghai
destinations.slope: Indoor: slopes for four levels, the longest 340 m at up to 26°
destinations.crowdNote: Chinese school holidays and summer weekends are very busy.
destinations.pitch: Certified by Guinness as the world's largest indoor ski resort when it opened in 2024: 90,000 m² of real snow, with ski-in, ski-out hotel rooms.
destinations.avalanche: None: it's indoors.
destinations.weather: Kept well below freezing inside; Shanghai summers are hot and humid outside.

destinations.name: Snowy Mountains (Thredbo, Perisher)
destinations.crowdNote: Sydney/Melbourne school holidays: very busy.
destinations.pitch: Australia's biggest areas; snowmaking-dependent, variable natural snow.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resorts, avalanche risk is low. In the backcountry: cornices and wind slabs on lee slopes, wet slides in spring.
destinations.weather: Marginal: rain and freeze-thaw are common.

destinations.name: Kosciuszko Main Range
destinations.pitch: Australia's alpine high point: day and overnight touring from Thredbo/Charlotte Pass; Western Faces.
destinations.avalanche: Cornices and wind slabs on lee slopes are the main problems; whiteouts and navigation are serious hazards too.
destinations.weather: Very changeable; whiteouts.

destinations.name: Victorian Alps (Falls Creek, Hotham, Buller)
destinations.pitch: Melbourne's playground; Hotham has the most expert terrain in Australia.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resorts, avalanche risk is low. In the backcountry: wind slabs and cornices on lee slopes, wet slides in spring.
destinations.weather: Marginal.

destinations.name: Queenstown & Wanaka
destinations.pitch: Four resorts (Remarkables, Coronet Peak, Cardrona, Treble Cone) and the adventure capital; heli everywhere.
destinations.avalanche: NZ maritime-transitional: storm and wind slabs; the snowpack usually stabilises quickly between storms.
destinations.weather: Big variability; nor'west winds.

children.name: Coronet Peak
children.note: Ikon. Closest to town, night skiing.

children.name: Treble Cone
children.note: Steepest and biggest in NZ's south.

destinations.name: Mt Hutt
destinations.crowdNote: Road closures on windy days.
destinations.pitch: Big open bowl above the Canterbury Plains; Methven heli nearby.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: storm and wind slabs after nor'west and southerly storms; big freeze-thaw swings make it icy.
destinations.weather: Wind-prone; often closed.

destinations.name: NZ Club Fields (Craigieburn, Broken River, Temple Basin)
destinations.pitch: Rope tows with nutcrackers, steep ungroomed terrain, club lodges. Unique and cheap.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime; uncontrolled terrain outside boundaries.
destinations.weather: Variable; NW storms.

destinations.name: Southern Alps Heli & Tasman Glacier
destinations.pitch: Big-day heli from Wanaka/Methven/Queenstown, and ski-plane runs on the Tasman Glacier under Aoraki.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime alpine: storm and wind slabs; glacier hazards on the Tasman. Heli operators run professional avalanche programs.
destinations.weather: Weather days are common.

destinations.name: Mt Ruapehu
destinations.pitch: Active volcano in the North Island with crater-lake ski touring; variable conditions.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime volcanic: rime ice and wind slabs; icy, wind-scoured terrain. Lahar hazard from the crater lake, too.
destinations.weather: Exposed, very variable.

destinations.name: Oukaïmeden
destinations.crowdNote: Marrakech day-trippers on weekends.
destinations.pitch: Ski Africa's highest lift-served slopes, an hour and a half from the Marrakech souks. Basic lifts, donkey 'lifts' and a big novelty factor.
destinations.avalanche: On piste, avalanche risk is low; snow cover is the bigger worry, as it is erratic year to year.
destinations.weather: Sunny; snow comes from a few Atlantic storms and can vanish fast.

destinations.name: Toubkal & High Atlas
destinations.pitch: Ski-tour North Africa's highest peak (4,167 m) from Berber villages and the Toubkal refuge, with mules carrying the gear.
destinations.avalanche: No forecasting service; wind slabs and icy spring snow.
destinations.weather: Unreliable snow years; sunny, cold nights.

destinations.name: Sierra Nevada (Granada)
destinations.crowdNote: Spanish weekends and holidays.
destinations.pitch: Europe's southernmost major resort: ski in the morning, Alhambra in the afternoon, and on clear days you can see Africa.
destinations.avalanche: On piste, avalanche risk is low. Off-piste: wind slabs and spring wet slides on steeper slopes.
destinations.weather: Very sunny; relies on snowmaking in dry years.

destinations.name: Crete: Lefka Ori
destinations.pitch: The White Mountains: ski-tour a lunar karst plateau with the Libyan Sea below, then eat in a taverna by the beach. Psiloritis is the other option.
destinations.avalanche: No forecasting service: wind slabs and spring wet-snow cycles on the high Lefka Ori. Go with local guides.
destinations.weather: Snow comes in short windows; very variable.

destinations.name: Mount Etna
destinations.pitch: Ski-tour an active volcano above the Mediterranean, through steaming vents and black ash; two small lift areas too.
destinations.avalanche: Volcanic hazards; summit access is regulated.
destinations.weather: Windy summit; snow often gets ash-covered.

destinations.name: Afriski
destinations.crowdNote: South African school holidays.
destinations.pitch: One of only two ski resorts in Southern Africa, at 3,000 m in the 'Kingdom in the Sky'. Small and snowmaking-based, but unique.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resort, avalanche risk is minimal: it is a small, gentle area.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry, sunny; little natural snow.

destinations.name: Ski Egypt
destinations.slope: Indoor: one main slope, about 210 m long
destinations.crowdNote: Busiest on Fridays, Saturdays and holidays.
destinations.pitch: Africa's first indoor ski slope, in a mall on the edge of Cairo: ski in the morning and see the Pyramids of Giza in the afternoon.
destinations.avalanche: None: it's indoors.
destinations.weather: Kept at about −2 °C inside, even when it's 40 °C outside.

destinations.name: Dizin & Shemshak
destinations.crowdNote: Tehran weekends (Thu-Fri).
destinations.pitch: High, dry Alborz powder an hour or two from Tehran: steep Shemshak, big open Dizin.
destinations.avalanche: Continental: wind slabs and persistent layers; limited public forecasting. Off-piste at Dizin and Shemshak is big terrain.
destinations.weather: Dry snow, sunny.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against travel to Iran, and dual nationals face particular risks. Check your government's current advice before planning.

destinations.name: Mount Damavand
destinations.pitch: Ski a 5,610 m volcano, the highest in Asia, from the Bargah-e Sevom hut: a big-altitude spring descent.
destinations.avalanche: High-altitude; fumaroles; altitude sickness is the main risk.
destinations.weather: Spring stability; high winds at the summit.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against travel to Iran, and dual nationals face particular risks. Check your government's current advice before planning.

destinations.name: Mzaar & The Cedars
destinations.crowdNote: Beirut weekends.
destinations.pitch: Ski in the morning, Mediterranean beach in the afternoon. The Cedars sits above an ancient cedar grove.
destinations.avalanche: On piste, avalanche risk is low. Off-piste: wind slabs and wet-snow cycles on open slopes.
destinations.weather: Wet Mediterranean storms; variable.

children.name: The Cedars
children.note: Highest, by the Cedars of God grove.

destinations.advisory: Advice for Lebanon changes quickly, and some areas are no-go. Check your government's current advice before planning.

destinations.name: Ski Dubai
destinations.slope: Indoor: five runs, the longest about 400 m with a drop of about 60 m
destinations.crowdNote: Busiest at weekends and in school holidays; weekday mornings are quietest.
destinations.pitch: Real snow inside a Dubai shopping mall, with a chairlift, a 400 m run and a colony of penguins. Pure novelty, and great fun as a stopover.
destinations.avalanche: None: it's indoors.
destinations.weather: Kept below freezing inside, whatever the desert heat outside.

destinations.name: Mauna Kea
destinations.pitch: Ski a 4,200 m tropical volcano by 4x4 shuttle, then surf the same day. Only after rare winter storms, so it's an opportunistic trip.
destinations.avalanche: Rocky and icy; high altitude; summit is sacred, so respect closures.
destinations.weather: Snow is rare and melts fast.

destinations.name: Wolf Creek
destinations.crowdNote: Remote: weekend Texans and New Mexicans, otherwise quiet.
destinations.pitch: The most snow in Colorado, an independent family-owned hill, and a cheap ticket. Pairs with Taos or Silverton.
destinations.avalanche: San Juan continental: one of the weakest snowpacks in the US, with deep persistent slabs. Heavy snowfall helps in-bounds.
destinations.weather: Big San Juan storms.

destinations.name: Winter Park & Mary Jane
destinations.crowdNote: Denver weekends; the ski train helps.
destinations.pitch: Denver's local giant: Mary Jane's famous bumps, Winter Park's cruisers, and a direct ski train from Union Station.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: faceted base layers and persistent slabs off-piste; in-bounds terrain is controlled.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry.

destinations.name: Ogden Valley (Snowbasin & Powder Mountain)
destinations.crowdNote: Far quieter than the Cottonwoods.
destinations.pitch: Uncrowded Utah: Snowbasin's Olympic terrain and lodges, and Powder Mountain's cap on daily ticket sales.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain: early-season facets can leave a buried persistent weak layer; the Utah Avalanche Center forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Utah powder.

destinations.name: Jotunheimen huts
destinations.crowdNote: Busy over Easter.
destinations.airport: Oslo, then 5h drive or train to Otta
destinations.pitch: Norway's highest mountains (Galdhøpiggen, Glittertind) on a DNT hut network: classic Easter and spring touring, glacier day trips from Juvasshytta and Spiterstulen.
destinations.avalanche: Continental-ish spring snowpack; varsom.no forecasts.
destinations.weather: Cold, clear spring highs; long days.

destinations.name: Bernese Oberland Haute Route
destinations.airport: Zurich / Bern by train to Jungfraujoch
destinations.pitch: Ride the train to the Jungfraujoch and tour the Aletsch glacier world between big huts (Konkordia, Finsteraarhorn): Switzerland's grandest hut tour.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Alps, glaciated high alpine: wind slabs and spring wet-snow cycles; crevasses on the glacier passes.
destinations.weather: High altitude weather windows.

destinations.name: Écrins huts
destinations.pitch: Big, wild glaciated massif around the Barre des Écrins, with the Dôme des Écrins as a classic 4,000 m ski summit. Wilder and quieter than Chamonix.
destinations.avalanche: Southern Alps: thinner snowpack, persistent layers.
destinations.weather: Sunny southern Alps.

destinations.name: Vanoise Haute Route
destinations.pitch: Hut-to-hut glacier traverse through France's first national park, between Pralognan and Val d'Isère.
destinations.avalanche: Inner Alps: persistent weak layers in thin winters, wind slabs, and spring wet-snow cycles; glaciers on parts of the route.

destinations.name: Stubai Alps huts
destinations.pitch: Austria's classic hut-touring week: dense hut network (Franz-Senn, Amberger), lots of 3,000 m summits, 40 minutes from Innsbruck.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Tyrol, glaciated: wind slabs and persistent layers; crevasses above the huts. avalanche.report forecasts daily.

destinations.name: Ortler & Cevedale
destinations.pitch: High glaciated touring from the Casati and Branca huts: Cevedale and Palon de la Mare are classic ski summits.
destinations.avalanche: Southern/inner Alps, glaciated: wind slabs and persistent layers in thin winters; crevasses and seracs on the big peaks.

destinations.name: Pyrenees Haute Route
destinations.pitch: Hut-to-hut across the central Pyrenees (Gavarnie to Aneto) with Spanish food and fewer people than the Alps.
destinations.avalanche: Pyrenees: wind slabs and wet-snow cycles; the snowpack can be thin on the Spanish side. Météo-France and AEMET forecast.
destinations.weather: Atlantic storms vs Mediterranean sun.

destinations.name: Wapta Icefield Traverse
destinations.pitch: The Rockies' classic hut-to-hut glacier traverse (Bow, Peyto, Balfour, Scott Duncan huts) off the Icefields Parkway.
destinations.avalanche: Rockies continental, glaciated: weak, faceted base layers, wind slabs on the icefield edges, and crevasses.
destinations.weather: Cold; spring stability.

destinations.name: Sierra High Route
destinations.pitch: The 'Sierra High Route': a committing 6-7 day spring traverse across the High Sierra near Mt Whitney, camping or tenting rather than huts.
destinations.avalanche: Spring Sierra: corn cycles with afternoon wet slides; big storm cycles can still bring storm slabs.
destinations.weather: Stable spring sun.

destinations.name: Tateyama Kurobe
destinations.pitch: Spring-only: the Alpine Route opens in mid-April to giant snow walls, giving access to huge Northern Alps couloirs from mountain huts at Murodo.
destinations.avalanche: Spring snowpack: wet-snow avalanches and cornice collapses as it warms; huge snow depths from winter.
destinations.weather: Clear spring weather; deep snowpack.

destinations.name: High Tatras
destinations.pitch: Compact granite range with steep couloirs and mountain huts (chaty), cheap and accessible from Kraków or Poprad.
destinations.avalanche: Continental; strict national park rules on routes.
destinations.weather: Cold, variable.

destinations.name: Sochi: Krasnaya Polyana
destinations.crowdNote: Busy Russian holidays (early Jan).
destinations.pitch: The 2014 Olympic cluster: big modern lift systems 1 hour from the Black Sea, with lots of tree and sidecountry terrain.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime Caucasus: heavy snowfall brings storm slabs; big, steep terrain off-piste at Rosa Khutor.
destinations.weather: Black Sea moisture brings big, wet dumps; the lower slopes can see rain.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

destinations.name: Elbrus Region (Cheget & Elbrus)
destinations.pitch: Old-school Soviet lifts on Cheget and the Elbrus cable car give huge, cheap freeride under Europe's highest peak.
destinations.avalanche: Caucasus continental; big avalanche paths, limited control.
destinations.weather: High and cold; storms close lifts.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

destinations.name: Mount Elbrus Summit Descent
destinations.crowdNote: Busy with climbers in summer, quiet in spring.
destinations.pitch: Ski off the highest summit in Europe (5,642 m): a spring acclimatisation expedition with one of the world's great volcano descents.
destinations.avalanche: High altitude, crevasses, ice; whiteouts are the classic killer.
destinations.weather: Severe summit winds and cold; tight weather windows.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

destinations.name: Dombai & Arkhyz
destinations.pitch: Dramatic Caucasus peaks (Dombai) and a fast-growing modern resort (Arkhyz, voted Russia's best). Cheap, with big off-piste.
destinations.avalanche: Caucasus: heavy snowfall with storm and wind slabs; steep terrain and limited forecasting. Go with local guides.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

destinations.name: Khibiny (Kirovsk)
destinations.pitch: Arctic freeride and touring above the Kola Peninsula: open bowls, a long spring season, and midnight sun in May.
destinations.avalanche: Arctic; well-known avalanche centre in Kirovsk; wind slabs.
destinations.weather: Polar night in Dec-Jan; spring is best.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

destinations.name: Sheregesh
destinations.crowdNote: Famous party weekends.
destinations.pitch: Siberia's powder capital: deep, very cold, dry snow in birch and fir forests, with a famous spring party scene.
destinations.avalanche: Mostly tree skiing; cold continental snowpack.
destinations.weather: Very cold (−25 °C is normal); deep snow.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

destinations.name: Almaty: Shymbulak backcountry
destinations.crowdNote: City weekends at Shymbulak.
destinations.pitch: A gondola from a big, cheap city straight into the Tian Shan: lift-served freeride above Shymbulak and a 4,000 m wall rising behind Almaty.
destinations.avalanche: Continental Tian Shan: significant avalanche risk and limited rescue.
destinations.weather: Sunny, cold, dry snow.

children.name: Shymbulak
children.note: The main resort, gondola from the city.

destinations.name: Trans-Ili Alatau huts & yurts
destinations.pitch: Multi-day touring from yurts, mountain huts and an old Soviet observatory: Bogdanovich Glacier above Shymbulak, the Turgen Gorge, and the Ketmen ridge to the east.
destinations.avalanche: Continental; deep weak layers; very limited rescue.
destinations.weather: Dry, cold, sunny between storms.

destinations.name: Fanes-Senes-Braies (Dolomites)
destinations.pitch: Quiet Dolomites touring through a nature park of limestone plateaus, with excellent rifugi (Fanes, Lavarella) between Cortina and Alta Badia.
destinations.avalanche: Southern Alps: often thin, faceted snowpack with persistent weak layers; wind slabs in the high cirques.
destinations.weather: Sunny; depends on southern storms.

destinations.name: Baffin Island (Clyde River & Sam Ford Fjord)
destinations.crowdNote: A handful of teams each spring.
destinations.pitch: Big-wall fjords and 1,000 m couloirs straight off the sea ice, from tent camps reached by Inuit-run snowmobile.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; cold, dry high-arctic snowpack. Self-reliance and polar-bear protection required.
destinations.weather: Very cold in April, milder in May; 24-hour daylight by mid-May.

children.name: Ruth Gorge (Sheldon Amphitheater)
children.note: Glacier ski touring from a fly-in base camp.

destinations.name: Denali & Ruth Gorge
destinations.crowdNote: Busy West Buttress camps in late May; Ruth Gorge is quiet.
destinations.pitch: North America's highest peak, guided on skis since 2022, or glacier ski touring under the granite walls of Ruth Gorge.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast; glacier travel and crevasse rescue skills essential.
destinations.weather: Extreme cold and wind high up; storms can pin teams for days.

destinations.name: Mera Peak
destinations.crowdNote: A popular trekking peak; skiers are few.
destinations.pitch: The Himalaya's classic ski objective: a gentle glacier from 6,476 m with Everest, Lhotse and Makalu on the horizon.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; guides manage glacier and altitude risk.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry and stable in the pre- and post-monsoon windows.

destinations.name: Annapurna Sanctuary
destinations.crowdNote: Trekkers on the trail; nobody on skis.
destinations.pitch: Ski touring inside a ring of 7,000 and 8,000 m peaks from the lodges at Annapurna Base Camp.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; the sanctuary approach is notorious for avalanche paths.
destinations.weather: Cold clear mornings, afternoon cloud; late-winter snow.

destinations.name: Muztagh Ata
destinations.crowdNote: A few commercial teams each July.
destinations.pitch: The 7,546 m 'father of ice mountains': the classic first 7,000 m peak to ski, with a broad glacier from near the summit.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; high-altitude glacier travel.
destinations.weather: Thin air, strong sun, sudden storms; summer is the stable window.
destinations.advisory: Xinjiang has pervasive police checkpoints and surveillance; border areas (including Hemu/Kanas and the Pamir) need extra permits, and some travellers also weigh the region's human-rights situation. Check your government's travel advice.

children.name: Cotopaxi
children.note: 5,897 m; access depends on volcanic activity.

children.name: Chimborazo
children.note: 6,263 m; farthest point from Earth's centre.

destinations.name: Ecuador's Volcanoes (Cayambe, Cotopaxi, Chimborazo)
destinations.crowdNote: Climbers on the standard routes; few skiers.
destinations.pitch: Ski glaciated volcanoes on the equator, ending on Chimborazo: the point on Earth farthest from its centre.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; rime ice, crevasses and quick melt-freeze cycles.
destinations.weather: Equatorial: no real seasons, but drier windows; altitude is the challenge.

destinations.name: Mount Ararat
destinations.crowdNote: Very few ski parties.
destinations.pitch: Ski the 5,137 m volcano where Noah's Ark is said to rest, with mule support to camp and views into Iran and Armenia.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; open, mostly moderate slopes.
destinations.weather: Cold, windy summit days; best snow March–April.
destinations.advisory: Ararat is a military border zone: a climbing permit through a licensed Turkish agency is required and takes weeks. Check your government's advice for eastern Türkiye.

destinations.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
destinations.crowdNote: Remote; you will see your own team.
destinations.pitch: Ski onto the largest ice field outside the poles, under the east faces of Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; glacier travel and storm-proof camping essential.
destinations.weather: Infamous wind and storms; good-weather windows are short and precious.

destinations.name: Greenland Ice Cap Crossing
destinations.crowdNote: A few dozen teams a year.
destinations.pitch: The classic polar journey: about 550 km and four weeks pulling a sled across the ice cap, coast to coast.
destinations.avalanche: Not an avalanche trip; crevasses near the coasts, piteraq storms and cold injury are the risks.
destinations.weather: −30 °C nights in spring; katabatic storms.

destinations.name: Vatnajökull Crossing
destinations.crowdNote: A few guided groups each spring.
destinations.pitch: Europe's largest ice cap on skis: a week-plus pulling sleds over volcanoes buried under the ice.
destinations.avalanche: Low avalanche exposure; crevasses, whiteout and storms are the risks.
destinations.weather: Fast-moving Atlantic storms; long spring days.

destinations.name: Sarek
destinations.crowdNote: Roadless and hutless: true solitude.
destinations.pitch: Sweden's wildest park: no huts, no roads, no trails, a week of tent and sled touring among glaciated peaks.
destinations.avalanche: Swedish avalanche forecasts cover nearby areas; steep valley sides.
destinations.weather: Cold and windy; March–April brings light and stable days.

children.name: Jikepulin (Hemu)
children.note: 1,466 m vertical; Freeride World Tour qualifier venue.

children.name: Jiangjunshan
children.note: Town hill above Altay city; ancient ski rock art nearby.

destinations.name: Altay: Jikepulin-Hemu
destinations.crowdNote: Growing fast domestically; still quiet midweek.
destinations.pitch: Bone-dry powder in the hills that claim to be the birthplace of skiing, beside a Tuvan log-cabin village.
destinations.avalanche: Resort patrol closes high-risk zones; no public regional forecast.
destinations.weather: Very cold (−20 °C common); light, cold smoke snow.
destinations.advisory: Xinjiang has pervasive police checkpoints and surveillance; border areas (including Hemu/Kanas and the Pamir) need extra permits, and some travellers also weigh the region's human-rights situation. Check your government's travel advice.

destinations.name: Erciyes & Cappadocia
destinations.crowdNote: Busy on Turkish holidays only.
destinations.pitch: Ski an extinct 3,917 m volcano by day and sleep in a Cappadocian cave hotel among the balloons.
destinations.avalanche: Resort controlled; off-piste on open volcano slopes.
destinations.weather: Sunny, dry continental winters.

destinations.name: Amirsoy & Chimgan
destinations.crowdNote: Weekend crowds from Tashkent; quiet midweek.
destinations.pitch: New lifts and old Soviet runs in the Tian Shan, 90 minutes from Tashkent and a train ride from Samarkand.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast; off-piste and heli days with local guides.
destinations.weather: Continental, sunny; short season.

destinations.name: Popova Šapka Cat Skiing
destinations.crowdNote: Small groups, big terrain.
destinations.pitch: Europe's oldest cat-skiing operation, in the wild Šar Mountains above a small Balkan resort.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast; operators manage terrain.
destinations.weather: Balkan winter: storms from the Adriatic, then sun.

children.name: Bansko ski area
children.note: 75 km of pistes; the backup for stormy days.

destinations.name: Pirin & Bansko
destinations.crowdNote: Bansko is lively; the tours are quiet.
destinations.pitch: Alpine limestone peaks up to 2,914 m Vihren above a cheap, lively resort town: tour by day, lifts as backup.
destinations.avalanche: Bulgarian mountain rescue publishes avalanche info; marble and limestone slabs.
destinations.weather: Mediterranean-influenced: big snows, then sunny spells.

children.name: Kanin – Sella Nevea
children.note: Cross-border lift access to high karst terrain.

children.name: Triglav traverse
children.note: Hut-to-hut circuit around Slovenia's highest peak.

destinations.name: Julian Alps (Kanin & Triglav)
destinations.crowdNote: Busy weekends with locals.
destinations.pitch: Limestone karst peaks above emerald rivers: day tours from Kanin's lifts and a hut traverse around Triglav.
destinations.avalanche: Slovenian forecast (ARSO); limestone gullies and cornices.
destinations.weather: Big Adriatic storms; sunny clear spells.

destinations.name: Corsica: Alta Strada
destinations.crowdNote: A few guided groups per season.
destinations.pitch: The GR20 on skis: a week-long haute route along the granite spine of a Mediterranean island, with sea views.
destinations.avalanche: Météo-France bulletin for Corsica; variable cover year to year.
destinations.weather: Snow comes and goes fast; March is usually best.

destinations.name: Valle Maira
destinations.crowdNote: Popular with Europeans, but spread across hundreds of tours.
destinations.pitch: An Occitan valley with no lifts and hundreds of mapped tours, stone hamlets and some of the best food in the Alps.
destinations.avalanche: Southwestern Alps: often thin, faceted snowpack with persistent layers; the Piedmont regional bulletin (Arpa Piemonte) forecasts the valley.
destinations.weather: Southern Alps: sunnier than the north side, snow from Mediterranean storms.

children.name: Naltar ski area
children.note: Small lift area run by the Pakistan Air Force; touring above.

children.name: Hunza (Karimabad)
children.note: Village base for touring in the valley.

destinations.name: Hunza & Naltar
destinations.crowdNote: Almost no foreign skiers.
destinations.pitch: Ski touring under 7,000 m Karakoram giants, with Hunza's apricot-orchard villages and legendary hospitality.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast; big terrain, local guides essential.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry winters; flights to Gilgit are weather-dependent.
destinations.advisory: Several governments advise against travel to parts of Pakistan; Gilgit-Baltistan is generally treated differently from border regions. Check your government's current advice and use a registered local operator.

destinations.name: Altai Tavan Bogd
destinations.crowdNote: Kazakh herders and eagle hunters; few skiers.
destinations.pitch: Yurt-based ski touring on Mongolia's highest glaciers, hosted by Kazakh eagle-hunting families.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast service: cold, thin, wind-affected snowpack; glaciers and crevasses. Expedition-style, guided only.
destinations.weather: Brutally cold in winter; spring is the touring season.

destinations.name: Manali Heli (Himachal)
destinations.crowdNote: One operator, small groups.
destinations.pitch: Long-running heli skiing in the Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar ranges, with 1,000 m-plus runs from Himalayan ridges.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast: Himalayan wind and storm slabs on big terrain. The heli operator manages avalanche risk.
destinations.weather: Storms from the west, then clear cold spells.

destinations.name: Mount Fuji (spring)
destinations.crowdNote: A few dozen skiers on good May weekends.
destinations.pitch: Ski Japan's sacred volcano from the crater rim in late spring: a 1,500 m run with the whole country at your feet.
destinations.avalanche: Slush avalanches and hard icy slopes; falls are the main danger. Climbing plan required off-season.
destinations.weather: Wind and ice early; corn snow in May–June.

children.name: Nevis Range
children.note: Gondola to Aonach Mòr's freeride gullies.

destinations.name: Scottish Highlands (Cairngorms & Glencoe)
destinations.crowdNote: Busy with locals when it's good.
destinations.pitch: Wild, wind-scoured Highland plateaus and gullies, with whisky and bothies after; brilliant when it's on.
destinations.avalanche: Scottish Avalanche Information Service: cornices and wind slab.
destinations.weather: Famously fickle: storms, thaws and a few perfect days.

children.name: Lassen Peak
children.note: Spring volcano skiing once the park road opens.

destinations.name: Mount Shasta
destinations.crowdNote: Avalanche Gulch is busy on spring weekends; other sides are quiet.
destinations.pitch: A lone 4,322 m volcano with 2,000 m spring corn runs on every side, plus Lassen's volcano park 90 minutes away.
destinations.avalanche: Mount Shasta Avalanche Center; ice and rockfall high up.
destinations.weather: Corn cycles from April; summit wind and lenticular clouds.

children.name: Valhalla Range
children.note: Several lodges in the West Kootenay.

children.name: Kokanee & Kaslo area
children.note: Lodges reached from Nelson and Kaslo.

destinations.name: BC Backcountry Lodges (Selkirks & Kootenays)
destinations.crowdNote: One group per lodge, per week.
destinations.pitch: Fly in by helicopter to a timber lodge at treeline, then tour from the door for a week of Interior BC powder.
destinations.avalanche: Avalanche Canada; persistent weak layers are common.
destinations.weather: Cold interior storms, stable high-pressure spells.

destinations.name: Washington Pass (North Cascades)
destinations.crowdNote: Opening weekend of Hwy 20 is a party; quiet after.
destinations.pitch: Each spring the North Cascades Highway reopens onto a week's worth of granite couloirs and glacier lines.
destinations.avalanche: Cascade maritime: storm slabs in winter, then wet slides and cornices in spring. NWAC forecasts the area.
destinations.weather: Spring corn, with sun and storms in equal measure.

children.name: Gros Morne backcountry
children.note: Tablelands, Bonne Bay and the Long Range.

destinations.name: Gros Morne & Humber Valley
destinations.crowdNote: A small, friendly local scene.
destinations.pitch: Fjords, tablelands and treeless bowls in a UNESCO park, with Marble Mountain's lifts for stormy days.
destinations.avalanche: No regional forecast; Parks Canada info for Gros Morne.
destinations.weather: Atlantic maritime: lots of snow, lots of wind.
